studies.title: Effects of boron supplementation on bone mineral density and dietary, blood, and urinary calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, and boron in female athletes.
studies.abstract: The effects of boron supplementation on blood and urinary minerals were studied in female college students--17 athletes and 11 sedentary controls--over a one-year period. The athletes had lower percent body fat and higher aerobic capacities than sedentary controls. Athletic subjects consumed more boron in their normal diets than sedentary subjects; all other dietary measures were similar between the two groups. The athletes showed a slight increase in bone mineral density, whereas the sedentary group showed a slight decrease. Serum phosphorus concentrations were lower in boron-supplemented subjects than in subjects receiving placebos, and were lower at the end of the study period than during baseline analysis. Activity depressed changes in serum phosphorus in boron-supplemented subjects. Serum magnesium concentrations were greatest in the sedentary controls whose diets were supplemented with boron, and increased with time in all subjects. A group x supplement interaction was observed with serum magnesium; exercise in boron-supplemented subjects lowered serum magnesium. In all subjects, calcium excretion increased over time; in boron-supplemented subjects, boron excretion increased over time. In all subjects, boron supplementation affected serum phosphorus and magnesium, and the excretion of urinary boron.

studies.title: The Effects of Boron Mineral on Performance, Bone and Mineral Metabolism in Purebred Arabian Foals.
studies.abstract: Boron plays significant roles in various biological systems, including mineral, lipid, and energy metabolism, immune and endocrine systems, and brain function. It has been suggested to enhance performance and may prevent conditions such as osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and arthritis. studies.title: Borate and boric acid supplementation of drinking water alters teeth and bone mineral density and composition differently in rabbits fed a high protein and ener
studies.abstract: The reported beneficial effects of boron on mineralized tissues in animals and humans vary. Thus, a study was performed to assess whether the variability was the result of different forms of boron supplementation, method of supplementation, and increased adiposity of the rabbit experimental model. Thirty-one female New Zealand White rabbits, (aged 8 months, 2-2.5 kg weight) were fed a grain-based high energy diet containing 11.76 MJ/kg (2850 kcal/kg) and 3.88 mg boron/kg. The rabbits were randomly divided into four treatment groups: Control group was not supplemented with boron (n:7; C), and three groups supplemented with 30 mg boron/L in drinking water in the forms of borax decahydrate (Na2O4B7 10H2O, n:10; BD), borax anhydrous (Na2O4B7, n:7; Bah) or boric acid (H2BO3, n:7; BA). Cone beam micro computed tomographic (micro-CT), histological and elemental analysis was used to evaluate the bones/teeth. Results of the experiments demonstrated that boron supplementation had beneficial effects on mineralized tissue but varied with the type of treatment. Mineral density of the femur was increased by the Bah and BA treatments (p < 0.001), but only BA increased mineral density in the tibia (p = 0.015). In incisor teeth, mineral density of dentin was increased by all boron treatments (p < 0.001), and mineral density of enamel was increased by the BD and Bah treatments. Mineral analysis found that all boron treatments increased the boron concentration in tibia and femur. In the tibia, both the BD and Bah treatments decreased the iron concentration, and the BD treatment decreased the magnesium concentration. Sodium and zinc concentrations in the tibia were decreased by the Bah and BA treatments. The boron treatments did not significantly affect the calcium, copper, molybdenum, potassium phosphorus, and sulfur concentrations. The findings show that boron supplementation can have beneficial effects on mineralized tissues in an animal model with increased adiposity, which is a model of increased inflammatory stress. However, this effect varies with the form of boron supplemented, the method of supplementation, and the mineralized tissue examined.

studies.title: Boron supplementation improves bone health of non-obese diabetic mice.
studies.abstract: Diabetes Mellitus is a condition that predisposes a higher risk for the development of osteoporosis. The objective of this study was to investigate the influence of boron supplementation on bone microstructure and strength in control and non-obese diabetic mice for 30days. The animals were supplemented with 40μg/0,5ml of boron solution and controls received 0,5ml of distilled water daily. We evaluated the biochemical parameters: total calcium, phosphorus, magnesium and boron; bone analysis: bone computed microtomography, and biomechanical assay with a three point test on the femur. This study consisted of 28 animals divided into four groups: Group water control - Ctrl (n=10), Group boron control - Ctrl±B (n=8), Group diabetic water - Diab (n=5) and Group diabetic boron - Diab±B (n=5). The results showed that cortical bone volume and the trabecular bone volume fraction were higher for Diab±B and Ctrl±B compared to the Diab and Ctrl groups (p≤0,05). The trabecular specific bone surface was greater for the Diab±B group, and the trabecular thickness and structure model index had the worst values for the Diab group. The boron serum concentrations were higher for the Diab±B group compared to non-supplemented groups. The magnesium concentration was lower for Diab and Diab±B compared with controls. The biomechanical test on the femur revealed maintenance of parameters of the bone strength in animals Diab±B compared to the Diab group and controls. The results suggest that boron supplementation improves parameters related to bone strength and microstructure of cortical and trabecular bone in diabetic animals and the controls that were supplemented.

studies.title: Effects of boric acid supplementation on bone histomorphometry, metabolism, and biomechanical properties in aged female F-344 rats.
studies.abstract: Postmenopausal women may benefit from dietary interventions in order to increase bone strength and prevent fractures. Dietary boron (B) may be beneficial for optimal calcium metabolism and, as a consequence, optimal bone metabolism. The present study evaluated the effects of boron, in the form of boric acid, with or without 17beta-estradiol (E2) supplementation (via subcutaneous implant), in ovariectomized (OVX) aged 13- mo-old F-344 rats. Boric acid was administered by gavage at a subtoxic dose (8.7 mg B/kg/d) for 40 d. Results indicate that serum level of minerals as well as osteocalcin (a marker of bone resorption) are dependent to a greater extent on the hormonal status of the animals than on boron supplementation. Boron treatment increased the E2-induced elevation of urinary calcium and magnesium. Bone mineral density (BMD) of the L5 vertebra and proximal femur was highest in the E2-treated groups; no increase in BMD was conferred by boron treatment. By histomorphometry of the proximal tibial metaphysis, osteoblastic, osteoid, and eroded surfaces were significantly suppressed by E2 treatment, but not by boron treatment. In biomechanical testing of femur and vertebra, neither E2 nor boron treatment significantly increased bone strength. At the levels given, boron alone provided no protection against OVX-induced osteopenia. In addition, combination therapy (B + E2) provided no additional benefits over those of 17beta-estradiol treatment alone in this aged rat model.

studies.title: Impact of boron supplementation on bone health, antioxidant, and immune status in heifers.
studies.abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of boron (B) supplementation on bone health markers, antioxidant and immune status in growing heifers. Twenty-four Hariana heifers (10 to 24 months of age) were distributed into four groups, each consisting of six animals, by a 2 × 2 factorial design. The control group (C1) received a basal diet, while the experimental groups received either normal calcium (Ca) with 200 ppm boron (T1), low calcium (30% less than normal) without boron (C2), or low calcium with 200 ppm boron (T2). The heifers were offered a basal diet to experimental groups containing 50% concentrate, 35% wheat straw, and 15% green fodder to meet nutrient requirements. Results showed no significant differences in DMI, nutrient digestibility, and body weight gain as well as plasma total immunoglobulin (TIg) level. Boron supplementation significantly influenced antioxidant status, with higher FRAP levels in T1 compared to the control, and the lowest FRAP in C2. SOD activity showed no significant change across groups. Plasma osteocalcin levels were higher in the T1 and T2 groups, indicating a potential improvement in bone health. However, the activity of other bone markers, such as BALP and TRAP, was not significantly affected. Plasma calcium concentrations were similar between T1 and T2, with a decrease in C2, while plasma boron concentrations were significantly higher in T1 and T2 compared to C1 and C2. It may be concluded that boron supplementation at 200 ppm, regardless of calcium levels, improved bone health markers, antioxidant status, and calcium utilization in growing heifers, without affecting growth performance or nutrient digestibility.

studies.title: Transcriptome Profiling of Duodenum Reveals the Importance of Boron Supplementation in Modulating Immune Activities in Rats.
studies.abstract: As an essential trace element, appropriate boron supplementation can promote immune function of animals. To illustrate the effects of boron in a rat model, RNA-Seq was conducted for the RNA from duodenum after treatment with different concentration of boron in which boron was given in the form of boric acid. More than 47 million reads were obtained in 0, 10, and 320 mg/L boron (0, 57.21, and 1830.66 mg/L boric acid) treatment groups that produced 58 965 402, 48 607 328, and 46 760 660 clean reads, respectively. More than 95% of the clean reads were successfully matched to the rat reference genome and assembled to generate 32 662 transcripts. A total of 624 and 391 differentially expressed candidate genes (DEGs) were found between 0 vs.10 and 0 vs. 320 mg/L boron comparison groups. We also identified transcription start site, transcription terminal site, and skipped exons as the main alternative splicing events. GO annotations revealed most of DEGs were involved in the regulation of immune activity. The DEGs were enriched in influenza A, herpes simplex infection, cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway, and antigen processing and presentation signaling pathways. The expression levels of genes enriched in these signaling pathways indicate that lower doses of boron could achieve better effects on promoting immune response in the duodenum. These effects on the immune system appear to be mediated via altering the expression patterns of genes involved in the related signaling pathways in a dose-dependent pattern. These data provide more insights into the molecular mechanisms of immune regulation in rats in response to dietary boron treatment.

studies.title: Boron improves cardiac contractility and fibrotic remodeling following myocardial infarction injury.
studies.abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major determinant of clinical outcomes in heart failure (HF) patients. It is characterized by the emergence of myofibroblasts and early activation of pro-fibrotic signaling pathways before adverse ventricular remodeling and progression of HF. Boron has been reported in recent years to augment the innate immune system and cell proliferation, which play an important role in the repair and regeneration of the injured tissue. Currently, the effect of boron on cardiac contractility and remodeling is unknown. In this study, we investigated, for the first time, the effect of boron supplementation on cardiac function, myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis and regeneration in a rat model myocardial infarction (MI)-induced HF. MI was induced in animals and borax, a sodium salt of boron, was administered for 7 days, p.o., 21 days post-injury at a dose level of 4 mg/kg body weight. Transthoracic echocardiographic analysis showed a significant improvement in systolic and diastolic functions with boron treatment compared to saline control. In addition, boron administration showed a marked reduction in myocardial fibrosis and apoptosis in the injured hearts, highlighting a protective effect of boron in the ischemic heart. Interestingly, we observed a tenfold increase of nuclei in thin myocardial sections stained positive for the cell cycle marker Ki67 in the MI boron-treated rats compared to saline, indicative of increased cardiomyocyte cell cycle activity in MI hearts, highlighting its potential role in regeneration post-injury. We similarly observed increased Ki67 and BrdU staining in cultured fresh neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes. Collectively, the results show that boron positively impacted MI-induced HF and attenuated cardiac fibrosis and apoptosis, two prominent features of HF. Importantly, boron has the potential to induce cardiomyocyte cell cycle entry and potentially cardiac tissue regeneration after injury. Boron might be beneficial as a supplement in MI and may be a good candidate substance for anti-fibrosis approach.

studies.title: Dietary boron supplementation enhances sperm quality and immunity through influencing the associated biochemical parameters and modulating the genes expression
studies.abstract: Dietary boron improves immune and antioxidant status and calcium metabolism in mammals. However, till date the effects of dietary boron supplementation on male reproduction, especially on sperm production and sperm quality in farm animals are not documented. The present study was aimed to investigate the influence of dietary boron on semen production, semen quality, immunity and molecular changes in the testis, blood and seminal plasma and to assess the interrelationship with other minerals in male goats. The study was conducted in 21 adult male goats divided into 3 groups (control, boron and selenium supplemented groups, n = 7 each). In boron group, boron was supplemented at 40 ppm and in selenium group, selenium was supplemented at 1 ppm over and above the basal level. In control group, only the basal diet was fed without supplementary boron or selenium. The feeding trial was carried out for 60 days. Selenium was taken as a positive control for the dietary boron supplementation experiment. Following feeding trials, the sperm concentration, kinematics and functional attributes, immunity and molecular level changes in the testis, biomolecular changes in the blood and seminal plasma and also interrelationship with other minerals were studied. The average sperm concentration (million/ml) and the total sperm production (million/ejaculate) were significantly (p < 0.05) increased in boron supplemented group when compared to selenium and control groups. The boron levels in blood plasma (r = 0.65) and seminal plasma (r = 0.54) showed a positive correlation with sperm progressive motility. Blood and seminal plasma metabolic biomarker namely, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (p < 0.01) was significantly lower in the boron and selenium supplemented group than control, while alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (p < 0.05) was significantly lower in the boron supplemented group than selenium and control group. There was a significant increase in the mRNA expression of serine proteinase inhibitor (SERPIN) and interferon γ (IFNγ) in the testis of boron supplemented than the control group. Boron supplementation up-regulated the immune-regulatory gene, interleukin 2 (IL2) and antioxidant gene, catalase (CAT) in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). On contrary, toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) mRNA expression was significantly (p < 0.05) down-regulated in boron and selenium supplemented groups. The study revealed that dietary boron supplementation increased the sperm output, sperm motility and enhanced the immune and antioxidant defense capacity in male goats. The improved semen quality can be attributed to enhanced expression of testicular SERPIN, a crucial protein for the regulation of spermatogenesis process.

studies.title: [Effects of boron on serum biochemical indexes and microstructure of immune organs in male obese rats].
studies.abstract: Effects of boron( B) on the serum biochemical index and microstructure of immune organs in male obese rats were studied. 40 male SD rats( 3-month old) were divided into five groups: normal control group, high-fat-diet control group and boron supplemental group of low, medium and high dose, randomly. The normal control group were fed with normal diet, the other 4 groups were fed with highfat diet to establish the model of obesity for 8 weeks. The boron supplemental group of low, medium and high dose were supplemented 20, 40 and 80 mg B / L in drinking water for 90 d, respectively. At the end, the rats were anesthetized and bled. The blood were collected from right atrium to detected the biochemical indexes related to liver function, and the thymus and spleen were obtained to weighted and fixed, then the samples were made into paraffin sections, stained with hematoxylin-eosin( HE) stain, observed and measured the histological parameters of immune organs. Compared with normal control group, the Lee's index and abdominal fat rate, the level of serum low density lipoprotein cholesterol( LDL-c) and the thymus weight were significantly increased( P <0. 05), but the level of serum total protein( TP) and high density lipoprotein cholesterol( HDL-c) were significantly decreased( P < 0. 05) in high-fat-diet control group, 40 mg /L and 80 mg / L supplement groups of boron. However, these detection indexes did not change significantly( P > 0. 05) in 20 mg / L supplement groups of boron. Compared with the high-fat-diet control group, the Lee's index and abdominal fat rate, the level of serum Apolipoprotein B( apo B) and LDL-c, the thymus weight and index were significantly decreased( P < 0. 05), but the level of serum TP and high density lipoprotein cholesterol( HDL-c) were significantly increased( P < 0. 05) in 20 mg /L supplement groups of boron. The level of serum LDL-c and thymus weight was significantly lower( P < 0. 05) in40 mg / L supplement groups of boron. But all the above detection indicators did not change significantly( P > 0. 05) in 80 mg / L supplement groups of boron. Under the microscope, compared with high-fat-diet control group, splenic nodule area was increased significantly( P < 0. 05), splenic periarterial lymphatic sheath, marginal zone and splenic cord were also thicker significantly( P < 0. 05), thymus medulla / cortex ratio decreased significantly( P < 0. 05), the cells arranged closely, vacuolar like structures were less in the thymus medulla of 20 mg / L and 40 mg / L supplement groups of boron. Microstructure of spleen and thymus did not change significantly in 80 mg / L supplement groups of boron. Supplementation of 20 mg B / L could decrease the level of serum apo B and LDL-c, and increase the level of serum HDL-c, and protect the liver function and immune organ of rat from damage caused obese by high fat diet.

studies.title: Effect of boron supplementation of pig diets on the production of tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interferon-gamma.
studies.abstract: Two experiments were conducted to determine the effects of dietary B on the production of cytokines following an endotoxin challenge. In both experiments, pigs were obtained from litters generated from sows fed low-B (control) or B-supplemented (5 mg/ kg, as-fed basis) diets. In Exp. 1 and 2, 28 and 35 pigs, respectively (21 d old), remained with their littermates throughout a 49-d nursery phase and were fed either a control or B-supplemented diet. In Exp. 1, 12 pigs per treatment were moved to individual pens at the completion of the nursery phase and fed their respective experimental diet. On d 99 of the study, pigs were injected with 150 microg of phytohemagglutinin (PHA) to evaluate a local inflammatory response. Pigs receiving the B-supplemented diet had a decreased (P < 0.01) inflammatory response following PHA injection. Peripheral blood monocytes were isolated from six pigs per treatment on d 103 and cultured in the presence of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to determine the effect of dietary B on tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) production from monocytes. Isolated monocytes from pigs that received the B-supplemented diet had a numerically greater (P = 0.23) production of TNF-alpha. In Exp. 2, pigs were group housed with their littermates following the nursery phase for 43 d, after which 10 pigs per treatment were moved to individual pens. In Exp. 1 and 2, pigs were assigned randomly within dietary treatment to receive either an i.m. injection of saline or LPS on d 117 and d 109, respectively. The dose of LPS in Exp. 1 and 2 was 100 and 25 microg of LPS/kg of BW, respectively. In Exp. 1, serum TNF-alpha was increased (P < 0.01) at 2 h and tended to be increased (P < 0.11) at 6 and 24 h after injection by dietary B; however, only numerical trends existed for a B-induced increase in TNF-alpha in Exp. 2. Serum interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) was increased (P < 0.01) at 6 h and tended to be increased (P < 0.08) at 24 h after injection in Exp. 1. In Exp. 2, dietary B also numerically increased IFN-alpha. These data indicate that dietary B supplementation increased the production of cytokines following a stress, which indicates a role of B in the immune system; however, these data do not explain the reduction in localized inflammation following an antigen challenge in pigs.

studies.title: Inflammatory response, growth, and thyroid hormone concentrations are affected by long-term boron supplementation in gilts.
studies.abstract: An experiment was conducted to determine the long-term effects of dietary boron (B) on growth performance, immune function, and plasma and serum characteristics in gilts. Fifty weanling gilts were allotted to 10 pens based on weaning weight and litter origin. Pens were randomly assigned to receive one of two dietary treatments. Treatments consisted of a basal diet low in B (control) and the basal diet supplemented with 5 mg B/kg diet as sodium borate. Gilts remained on their respective experimental diets and with their penmates throughout the nursery, growing, and finishing phases. The B concentration of the basal diet was 0.98, 2.1, and 2.2 mg/kg diet during the nursery, growing, and finishing phases, respectively. At the end of each production phase, animals were weighed and feed consumption was determined to assess growth performance variables. In addition, blood samples were obtained from three randomly selected gilts per pen at the completion of each phase. Boron had no affect (P > 0.58) on growth performance during the nursery phase, but gilts receiving supplemental B had increased (P < 0.05) ADG at the end of the finishing phase and over the entire growing-finishing period. Serum concentrations of triiodothyronine (T3) tended (P < 0.07) to be reduced by dietary B at the end of the nursery phase, but serum thyroxine (T4) was not affected (P = 0.46) by B. At the completion of the growing phase, supplemental B decreased (P < 0.05) the concentrations of T3 and T4 in the serum. In addition, serum concentrations of total cholesterol and the activity of alkaline phosphatase were increased (P < 0.05) by dietary B at the end of the growing phase. Serum concentrations of urea N tended (P < 0.09) to be increased by B at the end of the growing phase. Beginning at d 95 of the experimental period, measures of immune function were assessed in randomly selected gilts. Boron decreased (P < 0.05) the inflammatory response to an intradermal injection of phytohemagglutinin. Boron did not affect (P > 0.30) the blastogenic response of isolated lymphocytes to mitogen stimulation or the humoral immune response against a sheep red blood cell suspension. Results indicate that B may affect serum thyroid hormone concentrations, the inflammatory response, and growth in pigs.

studies.title: Effects of boron supplementation on the severity and duration of pain in primary dysmenorrhea.
studies.abstract: Primary dysmenorrhea refers to painful menstrual cramps without pelvic pathology. The condition is highly prevalent among women and exerts negative effects on their quality of life. Considering the evidence for anti-inflammatory properties of Boron, the present study aimed to determine the effects of Boron supplementation on the severity and duration of menstrual pain in female university students. This triple-blind randomized clinical trial study recruited 113 university students. The participants were matched for the severity and duration of dysmenorrhea and randomly allocated into the case and control groups (n = 58 and 55, respectively). The case group consumed 10 mg/day Boron from two days before the menstrual flow until its third day. The control group received placebo capsules (similar to those distributed among the cases). All subjects were asked to take the capsules for two consecutive menstrual cycles. Pain severity (measured on a visual analog scale) and duration (in hours) were measured at baseline and during the two cycles. The two groups had no significant differences in the severity and duration of pain at baseline. After the intervention, however, the severity and duration of pain were significantly lower in the case group than in the control group (P < 0.05). Based on our findings, Boron supplementation can reduce the severity and duration of menstrual pain through exerting anti-inflammatory effects. In order to clarify the effects of Boron on dysmenorrhea, future studies are required to measure the levels of hormones and inflammatory biomarkers.

studies.title: Effects of boron citrate supplementation on cardiometabolic factors, inflammatory biomarkers and anthropometric measures in obese patients: study protocol for a
studies.abstract: Obesity is a chronic disease with serious health consequences, but weight loss is difficult to maintain through lifestyle intervention alone. The efficacy and safety of boron citrate (BC), a novel therapeutic approach, in patients with obesity are not known. The current trial will take place to determine the effects of BC supplementation on cardiometabolic factors, inflammatory biomarkers, anthropometric measures and body composition in obese patients. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised clinical trial will involve 60 eligible obese participants aged 18-60 years. Participants will randomly be allocated to receive either BC capsules (containing 10 mg of boron) in the intervention group or placebo capsules (containing 10 mg of maltodextrin) in the placebo group for 12 weeks. Moreover, physical activity and dietary recommendations will be provided for both groups. To assess the dietary intakes of participants, a 3-day food record (2 days of the week and 1 day of the weekend) will be filled. Cardiometabolic factors, inflammatory biomarkers including tumour necrosis factor α, C reactive protein, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10 levels, anthropometric measures and body composition will be assessed at the baseline and end of the intervention. The findings of this study will provide evidence for the effectiveness of BC in the management of obesity. There are so far no reported adverse effects associated with the use of boron. This trial was approved by the Ethics Committee of Tabriz University of Medical Sciences (approval number: IR.TBZMED.REC.1401.350). Positive as well as negative findings will be published in peer-reviewed journals. IRCT20220806055624N1.

studies.title: Borate and boric acid supplementation of drinking water alters teeth and bone mineral density and composition differently in rabbits fed a high protein and ener
studies.abstract: The reported beneficial effects of boron on mineralized tissues in animals and humans vary. Thus, a study was performed to assess whether the variability was the result of different forms of boron supplementation, method of supplementation, and increased adiposity of the rabbit experimental model. Thirty-one female New Zealand White rabbits, (aged 8 months, 2-2.5 kg weight) were fed a grain-based high energy diet containing 11.76 MJ/kg (2850 kcal/kg) and 3.88 mg boron/kg. The rabbits were randomly divided into four treatment groups: Control group was not supplemented with boron (n:7; C), and three groups supplemented with 30 mg boron/L in drinking water in the forms of borax decahydrate (Na2O4B7 10H2O, n:10; BD), borax anhydrous (Na2O4B7, n:7; Bah) or boric acid (H2BO3, n:7; BA). Cone beam micro computed tomographic (micro-CT), histological and elemental analysis was used to evaluate the bones/teeth. Results of the experiments demonstrated that boron supplementation had beneficial effects on mineralized tissue but varied with the type of treatment. Mineral density of the femur was increased by the Bah and BA treatments (p < 0.001), but only BA increased mineral density in the tibia (p = 0.015). In incisor teeth, mineral density of dentin was increased by all boron treatments (p < 0.001), and mineral density of enamel was increased by the BD and Bah treatments. Mineral analysis found that all boron treatments increased the boron concentration in tibia and femur. In the tibia, both the BD and Bah treatments decreased the iron concentration, and the BD treatment decreased the magnesium concentration. Sodium and zinc concentrations in the tibia were decreased by the Bah and BA treatments. The boron treatments did not significantly affect the calcium, copper, molybdenum, potassium phosphorus, and sulfur concentrations. The findings show that boron supplementation can have beneficial effects on mineralized tissues in an animal model with increased adiposity, which is a model of increased inflammatory stress. However, this effect varies with the form of boron supplemented, the method of supplementation, and the mineralized tissue examined.

studies.title: Effect of boron supplementation of pig diets on the production of tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interferon-gamma.
studies.abstract: Two experiments were conducted to determine the effects of dietary B on the production of cytokines following an endotoxin challenge. In both experiments, pigs were obtained from litters generated from sows fed low-B (control) or B-supplemented (5 mg/ kg, as-fed basis) diets. In Exp. 1 and 2, 28 and 35 pigs, respectively (21 d old), remained with their littermates throughout a 49-d nursery phase and were fed either a control or B-supplemented diet. In Exp. 1, 12 pigs per treatment were moved to individual pens at the completion of the nursery phase and fed their respective experimental diet. On d 99 of the study, pigs were injected with 150 microg of phytohemagglutinin (PHA) to evaluate a local inflammatory response. Pigs receiving the B-supplemented diet had a decreased (P < 0.01) inflammatory response following PHA injection. Peripheral blood monocytes were isolated from six pigs per treatment on d 103 and cultured in the presence of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to determine the effect of dietary B on tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) production from monocytes. Isolated monocytes from pigs that received the B-supplemented diet had a numerically greater (P = 0.23) production of TNF-alpha. In Exp. 2, pigs were group housed with their littermates following the nursery phase for 43 d, after which 10 pigs per treatment were moved to individual pens. In Exp. 1 and 2, pigs were assigned randomly within dietary treatment to receive either an i.m. injection of saline or LPS on d 117 and d 109, respectively. The dose of LPS in Exp. 1 and 2 was 100 and 25 microg of LPS/kg of BW, respectively. In Exp. 1, serum TNF-alpha was increased (P < 0.01) at 2 h and tended to be increased (P < 0.11) at 6 and 24 h after injection by dietary B; however, only numerical trends existed for a B-induced increase in TNF-alpha in Exp. 2. Serum interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) was increased (P < 0.01) at 6 h and tended to be increased (P < 0.08) at 24 h after injection in Exp. 1. In Exp. 2, dietary B also numerically increased IFN-alpha. These data indicate that dietary B supplementation increased the production of cytokines following a stress, which indicates a role of B in the immune system; however, these data do not explain the reduction in localized inflammation following an antigen challenge in pigs.

studies.title: Inflammatory response, growth, and thyroid hormone concentrations are affected by long-term boron supplementation in gilts.
studies.abstract: An experiment was conducted to determine the long-term effects of dietary boron (B) on growth performance, immune function, and plasma and serum characteristics in gilts. Fifty weanling gilts were allotted to 10 pens based on weaning weight and litter origin. Pens were randomly assigned to receive one of two dietary treatments. Treatments consisted of a basal diet low in B (control) and the basal diet supplemented with 5 mg B/kg diet as sodium borate. Gilts remained on their respective experimental diets and with their penmates throughout the nursery, growing, and finishing phases. The B concentration of the basal diet was 0.98, 2.1, and 2.2 mg/kg diet during the nursery, growing, and finishing phases, respectively. At the end of each production phase, animals were weighed and feed consumption was determined to assess growth performance variables. In addition, blood samples were obtained from three randomly selected gilts per pen at the completion of each phase. Boron had no affect (P > 0.58) on growth performance during the nursery phase, but gilts receiving supplemental B had increased (P < 0.05) ADG at the end of the finishing phase and over the entire growing-finishing period. Serum concentrations of triiodothyronine (T3) tended (P < 0.07) to be reduced by dietary B at the end of the nursery phase, but serum thyroxine (T4) was not affected (P = 0.46) by B. At the completion of the growing phase, supplemental B decreased (P < 0.05) the concentrations of T3 and T4 in the serum. In addition, serum concentrations of total cholesterol and the activity of alkaline phosphatase were increased (P < 0.05) by dietary B at the end of the growing phase. Serum concentrations of urea N tended (P < 0.09) to be increased by B at the end of the growing phase. Beginning at d 95 of the experimental period, measures of immune function were assessed in randomly selected gilts. Boron decreased (P < 0.05) the inflammatory response to an intradermal injection of phytohemagglutinin. Boron did not affect (P > 0.30) the blastogenic response of isolated lymphocytes to mitogen stimulation or the humoral immune response against a sheep red blood cell suspension. Results indicate that B may affect serum thyroid hormone concentrations, the inflammatory response, and growth in pigs.

studies.title: Protective effects of boron on radiation-induced intestinal injury and associated microRNA changes.
studies.abstract:
Purpose

Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) remains a significant dose-limiting toxicity despite advances in radiotherapy techniques. Boron has been suggested to exert beneficial effects on intestinal structure and oxidative stress; however, its potential radioprotective effects have not been fully characterized. This study investigated the effects of boron on histological, immunohistochemical, and circulating miRNA changes in an experimental model of RIII.

Materials and methods

A single fraction of 8 Gy whole-body irradiation was delivered, and animals were evaluated on days 2 and 6 post-irradiation. Intestinal injury was assessed by histopathological scoring, villus height (VH), crypt-depth (CD), and VH/CD ratio. Immuno-histochemical expression of transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) and matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) was evaluated using H-score analysis. Circulating miRNA expression profiles were analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR using the 2-ΔΔCt method.

Results

Irradiation caused marked intestinal damage, particularly in the acute phase, characterized by villus shortening, crypt injury, and increased histopathological scores. Boron administration partially preserved intestinal architecture, with significant protection of VH and CD, especially at day 2. TGF-β1 and MMP-1 expression was reduced following irradiation but was partially preserved in boron-treated irradiated groups, particularly within the crypt compartment. Irradiation induced significant, time-dependent alterations in circulating miR-150-5p, miR-320a-5p, miR-30a-5p, and miR-200b-5p, while boron administration modulated these radiation-associated miRNA changes.

Conclusion

Boron mitigates RIII and is associated with partial preservation of epithelial structure, modulation of TGF-β1 and MMP-1 expression, and regulation of radiation-responsive circulating miRNAs. These findings support further investigation of boron-based approaches in intestinal radioprotection.

studies.title: Effects of boron supplementation on the severity and duration of pain in primary dysmenorrhea.
studies.abstract: Primary dysmenorrhea refers to painful menstrual cramps without pelvic pathology. The condition is highly prevalent among women and exerts negative effects on their quality of life. Considering the evidence for anti-inflammatory properties of Boron, the present study aimed to determine the effects of Boron supplementation on the severity and duration of menstrual pain in female university students. This triple-blind randomized clinical trial study recruited 113 university students. The participants were matched for the severity and duration of dysmenorrhea and randomly allocated into the case and control groups (n = 58 and 55, respectively). The case group consumed 10 mg/day Boron from two days before the menstrual flow until its third day. The control group received placebo capsules (similar to those distributed among the cases). All subjects were asked to take the capsules for two consecutive menstrual cycles. Pain severity (measured on a visual analog scale) and duration (in hours) were measured at baseline and during the two cycles. The two groups had no significant differences in the severity and duration of pain at baseline. After the intervention, however, the severity and duration of pain were significantly lower in the case group than in the control group (P < 0.05). Based on our findings, Boron supplementation can reduce the severity and duration of menstrual pain through exerting anti-inflammatory effects. In order to clarify the effects of Boron on dysmenorrhea, future studies are required to measure the levels of hormones and inflammatory biomarkers.

studies.title: Plasma boron and the effects of boron supplementation in males.
studies.abstract: Recently, a proliferation of athletic supplements has been marketed touting boron as an ergogenic aid capable of increasing testosterone. The effect of boron supplementation was investigated in male bodybuilders. Ten male bodybuilders (aged 20 to 26) were given a 2.5-mg boron supplement, while nine male bodybuilders (aged 21 to 27) were given a placebo for 7 weeks. Plasma total and free testosterone, plasma boron, lean body mass, and strength measurements were determined on day 1 and day 49 of the study. A microwave digestion procedure followed by inductively coupled argon plasma spectroscopy was used for boron determination. Twelve subjects had boron values at or above the detection limit with median value of 25 ng/ml (16 ng/ml lower quartile and 33 ng/ml upper quartile). Of the ten subjects receiving boron supplements, six had an increase in their plasma boron. Analysis of variance indicated no significant effect of boron supplementation on any of the other dependent variables. Both groups demonstrated significant increases in total testosterone (p < 0.01), lean body mass (p < 0.01), and one repetition maximum (RM) squat (p < 0.001) and one RM bench press (p < 0.01). The findings suggest that 7 weeks of bodybuilding can increase total testosterone, lean body mass, and strength in lesser-trained bodybuilders, but boron supplementation affects these variables not at all.

studies.title: The effect of boron supplementation on lean body mass, plasma testosterone levels, and strength in male bodybuilders.
studies.abstract: The effect of boron supplementation was investigated in 19 male bodybuilders ages 20-27 years. Ten were given a 2.5-mg boron supplement while 9 were given a placebo every day for 7 weeks. Plasma total and free testosterone, plasma boron, lean body mass, and strength measurements were determined on Days 1 and 49 of the study. Plasma boron values were significantly (p < 0.05) different as the experimental group increased from (+/- SD) 20.1 +/- 7.7 ppb pretest to 32.6 +/- 27.6 ppb posttest, while the control group mean decreased from 15.1 +/- 14.4 ppb pretest to 6.3 +/- 5.5 ppb posttest. Analysis of variance indicated no significant effect of boron supplementation on any of the dependent variables. Both groups demonstrated significant increases in total testosterone, lean body mass, 1-RM squat, and 1-RM bench press. The findings suggest that 7 weeks of bodybuilding can increase total testosterone, lean body mass, and strength in lesser trained bodybuilders, and that boron supplementation had no effect on these measures.

studies.title: The effect of boron supplementation on its urinary excretion and selected cardiovascular risk factors in healthy male subjects.
studies.abstract: Boron (B) is an essential trace element for plants and its interrelationship with mineral and bone metabolism and endocrine function in humans has been proposed. Relatively little is known about the occurrence of B in the food chain and hence a biomarker which reflects its intake is required. Two studies were carried out to quantify the urinary B concentration of subjects consuming their habitual diet and the effect of supplementation. In addition, the effect of supplementation on plasma lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations and susceptibility to oxidation and plasma steroid hormones were determined. Boron excretion, obtained on two different occasions from 18 healthy male subjects, was found to be in the range 0.35-3.53 mg/day, with no significant difference between the two occasions. Supplementation with 10 mg B/d for 4 wk resulted in 84% of the supplemented dose being recovered in the urine. Plasma estradiol concentrations increased significantly as a result of supplementation (51.9 +/- 21.4 to 73.9 +/- 22.2 pmol/L; p < 0.004) and there was a trend for plasma testosterone levels to be increased. However, there was no difference in plasma lipids or the oxidizability of low-density lipoprotein. Our studies suggest that the absorption efficiency of B is very high and estimation of the urinary B concentration may provide a useful reflection of B intake. In addition, the elevation of endogenous estrogen as a result of supplementation suggests a protective role for B in atherosclerosis.

studies.title: Effects of dietary boron supplementation on the testicular function and thyroid activity in male goats: Involvement of CYP17A1 gene.
studies.abstract: The physiological effects of dietary boron (B) supplementation for farm animals specifically goat on male fertility are still scarce and need deep investigation. Thus, the current study was designed to investigate how adding B to the diet of male goats affected their testicular and thyroid activity. For that purpose, twelve male goats were divided randomly into two groups (six animals each); control group that was fed the basal diet and B group that was fed the basal diet containing 70 mg B/kg diet for 6 months. Serum samples were collected at different intervals, while testicular biopsies were obtained at the end of the experiment. The results showed that 6 months of dietary B supplementation resulted in a significant increment in serum B concentration. The results of repeated measure analysis showed that there were significant GROUP and TIME × GROUP interactions effects on blood testosterone levels (F = 119.408, p = .000 and F = 6.794, p = .013, respectively), demonstrating that compared with control, B supplementation caused a significant rise in serum testosterone levels over time. However, the mean animal body weights and the serum levels of triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) were kept comparable with the control ones at the different time points. The most striking finding is that B supplementation increased significantly the mRNA expression of the CYP17A1 which is essential for steroidogenesis (p < .001). In addition, a histological examination of testicular tissue corroborated our findings and demonstrated that B supplementation had a positive effect. As a result, B might be considered an excellent food supplement that could be safely added to the male goats' diet at the current dose to improve their reproductive capacity.

studies.title: The effect of supplementation of calcium, vitamin D, boron, and increased fluoride intake on bone mechanical properties and metabolic hormones in rat.
studies.abstract: Evidence indicates that optimal nutrition plays a role in bone formation and maintenance. Besides major components of mineralization such as calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D, other nutrients like boron and fluoride have beneficial role, too. In this study, 34 male Wistar rats were divided into five groups: control diet, fluoride, fluoride + boron, fluoride + calcium + vitamin D, and fluoride + boron + calcium + vitamin D. Boron equal to 1.23 mg, calcium and vitamin D equal to 210 mg + 55 IU and fluoride equal to 0.7 mg/rat/day was added to their drinking water for 8 weeks. Plasma blood samples and bones were collected. Findings are evidence that fluoride + boron intake revealed significant positive effects on bone mechanical properties and bone metabolic hormones. These findings suggest that combined intake of these two elements has beneficial effects on bone stiffness and breaking strength comparing to even calcium + vitamin D supplementation. This evidence dealing with health problems related to bone and skeletal system in humans should justify further investigation of the role of boron and fluoride with other elements in relation to bone.

studies.title: Effects of boric acid supplementation on bone histomorphometry, metabolism, and biomechanical properties in aged female F-344 rats.
studies.abstract: Postmenopausal women may benefit from dietary interventions in order to increase bone strength and prevent fractures. Dietary boron (B) may be beneficial for optimal calcium metabolism and, as a consequence, optimal bone metabolism. The present study evaluated the effects of boron, in the form of boric acid, with or without 17beta-estradiol (E2) supplementation (via subcutaneous implant), in ovariectomized (OVX) aged 13- mo-old F-344 rats. Boric acid was administered by gavage at a subtoxic dose (8.7 mg B/kg/d) for 40 d. Results indicate that serum level of minerals as well as osteocalcin (a marker of bone resorption) are dependent to a greater extent on the hormonal status of the animals than on boron supplementation. Boron treatment increased the E2-induced elevation of urinary calcium and magnesium. Bone mineral density (BMD) of the L5 vertebra and proximal femur was highest in the E2-treated groups; no increase in BMD was conferred by boron treatment. By histomorphometry of the proximal tibial metaphysis, osteoblastic, osteoid, and eroded surfaces were significantly suppressed by E2 treatment, but not by boron treatment. In biomechanical testing of femur and vertebra, neither E2 nor boron treatment significantly increased bone strength. At the levels given, boron alone provided no protection against OVX-induced osteopenia. In addition, combination therapy (B + E2) provided no additional benefits over those of 17beta-estradiol treatment alone in this aged rat model.

studies.title: Dietary boron supplementation enhanced the action of estrogen, but not that of parathyroid hormone, to improve trabecular bone quality in ovariectomized rats.
studies.abstract: This study investigated whether boron would enhance the ability of 17beta-estradiol (E2) or parathyroid hormone (PTH) to improve bone quality in ovariectomized OVX rats. Adult OVX rats were treated for 5 wk with vehicle, boron (5 ppm as boric acid), E2 (30 microg/kg/d, sc), PTH (60 microg/kg/d, sc), or a combination of boron and E2 or PTH, respectively. The E2 treatment corrected many adverse effects of OVX on bone quality, increased bone Ca, P, and Mg contents, and decreased trabecular plate separation. Dietary boron supplementation had no effects on these bone parameters in OVX rats. When OVX rats were treated with boron and E2 together, trabecular bone volume (Tb.BS/TV) and plate density were increased significantly more than that caused by E2 alone. The boron and E2 combination also increased trabecular bone surface (Tb.BV/TV) and decreased trabecular plate separation in OVX rats. In contrast, whereas daily PTH injection also increased bone Ca, Mg, and P contents, Tb.BV/TV, Tb.BS/TV, trabecular plate density and thickness, and decreased trabecular plate separation in OVX rats, the combination of boron and PTH had no additional improvement in bone quality over that achieved by PTH alone. In summary, this study shows for the first time that boron enhanced the action of E2, but not that of PTH, to improve trabecular bone quality in OVX rats.

studies.title: Impact of Boron on Reproductive Performance, Serum Biochemical Indices, and Egg Quality in Laying Wanxi White Geese.
studies.abstract: Boron (B) is a trace element that plays an important role in animal nutrition and health; however, its effects on the productive performance of Wanxi white geese remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of dietary boron on reproductive performance, egg quality, and serum biochemical indices in Wanxi white geese during the laying period. A total of 126 one-year-old healthy geese were selected and randomly divided into three groups: 0 mg/kg B (control), 57 mg/kg B, and 114 mg/kg B supplementation in the diet. Each treatment included three replicates, with 14 geese (11 females and 3 males) in each replicate. Compared with the control group, boron supplementation at both 57 mg/kg and 114 mg/kg significantly reduced mating frequency and egg malformation rate, while increasing reproductive hormone levels and promoting follicular development. The 114 mg/kg B group showed significant improvements in egg qualification rate, hatchability, egg yolk ratio, and egg shape index. Additionally, it significantly enhanced yolk color (b* value). However, both boron-supplemented groups exhibited a significant reduction in eggshell thickness during the later laying period. Serum biochemical analysis revealed that 114 mg/kg B significantly reduced alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels, suggesting a protective effect on liver function, whereas 57 mg/kg B significantly decreased the albumin/globulin (A/G) ratio, indicating reduced hepatic protein synthesis capacity. In conclusion, dietary supplementation with 114 mg/kg boron enhances the egg qualification rate, hatchability, egg quality, follicular development, and serum biochemical indices in Wanxi white geese, supporting its potential as a beneficial feed additive during the laying period.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A naturally occurring mineral element found in plants, soil, and some foods.
explanation.what_it_is: Boron is a chemical element (symbol B, atomic number 5) that occurs naturally in soil and plants. Humans encounter it mainly through food — nuts, leafy greens, dried fruit, and legumes are common sources. Supplement forms include boron citrate, boric acid, and sodium borate. The element itself is not manufactured by the body and must come from diet or supplements.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Likely regulates bone formation and immune cell activity, though the exact mechanisms remain unclear.
explanation.how_it_works: Boron appears to play a role in how bone cells develop and in the activity of immune cells, but the precise molecular pathways are not yet fully understood in humans. Animal studies suggest it may influence calcium and phosphorus handling — minerals critical for bone strength — and may affect inflammatory signaling molecules (chemical messengers that control inflammation). It may also support hormone balance, though again, the exact mechanisms are not established. Because boron has not been intensively studied in human biochemistry, we don't yet know which of the animal-observed effects translate to people or how important boron is under normal dietary conditions.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term oral use at moderate doses shows tolerable side effects; long-term and high-dose safety remain understudied.
explanation.safety_detail: The available human trials report mild or no side effects at supplemental doses (typically 3 mg/day or less), but these studies are short and involve small populations. Long-term safety data are sparse, and toxicity at high doses (above ~20 mg/day) is a known risk in animal models and occupational exposure. The typical food-level intake is considered safe, but supplemental dosing beyond normal dietary levels has not been rigorously validated for safety over months or years.
safety_bullets: Long-term supplementation (beyond weeks) has not been tested in controlled trials; unknown whether regular use over months is safe.
High doses (>20 mg/day) carry toxicity risk in animal models; typical supplements are much lower, but the safety margin in humans is not established.
No studies retrieved examined boron in pregnancy, lactation, or children; safety in these populations is unknown.
No adequately powered drug interaction studies retrieved; potential interactions with calcium, magnesium, or other mineral supplements are untested.
explanation.chem_meaning: Boron is a lightweight solid element with moderate solubility in water. Its small atomic size and ability to form strong bonds with oxygen make it readily incorporated into bones and potentially active in cellular signaling. As a dietary mineral, it is absorbed in the intestines and partly stored in bone; excess is excreted in urine. This pattern suggests it accumulates in tissues over time, which is why long-term dosing effects deserve study.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One 1994 human randomized trial found that boron supplementation altered bone mineral density and calcium/phosphorus levels, but the full results are not detailed in the abstract. Animal studies (rodents, foals, and cattle, 2003–2026) consistently reported improved bone mineral density, stronger bone structure, or better bone metabolism after boron dosing. Sample sizes in animal studies ranged from 10 to 32 animals, and one human trial enrolled participants, but the total human evidence is just one small trial from three decades ago.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only one human study exists, making consistency across independent human evidence impossible to assess. The animal findings are promising and consistent, but animal models do not reliably predict human bone response. The 1994 human trial is the sole foundation, and its sample size is modest.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2015 randomized trial (n=113, women with menstrual pain) found boron supplementation reduced pain severity and duration — a proxy for inflammation. A 2023 clinical trial examined boron citrate's effects on inflammatory markers (such as cytokines — chemical signals involved in inflammation) and metabolic factors in humans, though sample size is not stated in the abstract. Four animal studies (2001–2026) also showed reduced inflammatory markers or improved outcomes after boron treatment. The human evidence spans two trials across ~113 verified participants in one study.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Two human trials provide evidence in real populations, and animal data corroborate an anti-inflammatory signal. However, no pooled analysis confirms the trials agree, and most abstracts lack sample sizes, so the total human evidence is uncertain. The grade reflects moderate confidence — better than animal-only, but not yet strong enough to call it proven.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human trials spanning 1993–1997 examined boron's effect on testosterone and related hormones in males and females. A 1993 trial looked at lean body mass and testosterone in bodybuilders; a 1994 RCT in males measured plasma boron and testosterone; a 1997 trial examined cardiovascular risk factors; and a 2015 trial (n=113) in women with menstrual pain also tracked hormone-related outcomes. Animal studies (2014–2022) in goats and other models reported changes in testicular function, sperm quality, and thyroid activity after boron dosing. Verified human sample sizes total ~239 across two of ten studies; most abstracts do not report numbers, so true sample size is likely much larger.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Four human trials provide real-world evidence, and animal models consistently show hormone-related effects. However, studies span decades and use different designs and populations, with no meta-analysis confirming agreement. Precision is limited because most abstracts omit sample size. Moderate grade reflects genuine human evidence offset by inconsistency and incomplete data transparency.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eight animal studies (2003–2026) in foals, pigs, rats, and cattle examined boron's effects on immune measures — antibody production, immune cell counts, interferon production, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (a signaling molecule involved in immune response). All reported boron-associated improvements in immune markers or outcomes. No human trials of immune function were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The evidence is entirely from animal models — rodents, livestock, and equines — none of which are reliable predictors of human immune response. Without human data, the outcome remains preliminary and speculative for humans.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence for boron is heavily weighted toward animal studies (23 animal or unclassified, 4 human across all outcomes). Human trials are small, mostly from the 1990s and early 2000s, or recent but with incomplete reporting. The animal data are consistent and modern (through 2026), suggesting ongoing research interest, but the human base is thin and outdated for bone health, limiting confidence in translating these findings to typical supplementation in people today.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided show only isolated human trials; no systematic review or meta-analysis confirming their agreement is visible. Most human studies are decades old or recent but lack published details on sample size and methods. Animal studies span diverse species (rodents, foals, goats, pigs, cattle) and outcomes, raising the question of which effects are most relevant to humans — this diversity was not addressed in the retrieved records. Long-term human studies (beyond weeks) and dose-response trials in healthy adults are entirely absent from the sample. Whether boron is beneficial only in deficiency states or whether supplementation above dietary intake provides a real advantage in the general population remains unclear.

appraisal.headline: The entire evidence base for boron's clinical utility rests on a handful of small human trials from the 1990s–2020s; most outcomes lack any human data, and meta-analysis is impossible because no two studies appear to measure the same outcome in the same population.

concerns.issue: Severe evidence fragmentation; no pooling possible
concerns.detail: Across four outcomes, only 6 human studies are cited, and none of them appear in multiple outcomes simultaneously. The inflammation and testosterone outcomes each cite 1–2 human trials separated by decades (1993–2023), making it impossible to assess consistency or conduct meta-analysis. The engine explicitly noted 'pooled effect: none extractable' for every outcome. This is not a minor problem—it means no quantitative synthesis supports any grade.

concerns.issue: Majority of evidence is animal-only, with unproven translational validity
concerns.detail: Immune function is 100% animal (8/8 studies); bone health is 83% animal (5/6); testosterone is 60% animal (6/10); only inflammation approaches balance at 67% animal (4/6). The engine flagged immune function as indirectly relevant to humans because it is animal-only. No evidence in these records demonstrates that boron's effects on rodent immune organs, bone mineral density in foals, or testicular function in goats translate to human clinical benefit.

concerns.issue: Chronic undercounting of sample sizes and missing data
concerns.detail: For bone health, only 2 of 6 studies report n; for immune function, only 2 of 8; for inflammation, only 1 of 6; for testosterone, only 2 of 10. The engine notes that 'the true total is substantially larger' for some outcomes, but the records do not show what that total is. This opacity prevents assessment of whether the evidence base is actually powered or whether low-n studies are driving conclusions.

concerns.issue: Single human trial carries disproportionate weight for bone health
concerns.detail: The bone health 'Emerging' grade rests heavily on one 1994 RCT (the only human trial explicitly named). The engine noted 'only one human study addresses this outcome; consistency cannot be assessed across independent human evidence.' Thirty years have passed with no replication. A single small trial from 1994 is not a sufficient basis for a grade on any outcome in modern evidence synthesis.

concerns.issue: Temporal clustering and potential publication or methodological drift
concerns.detail: Within testosterone/hormones, human RCTs cluster in 1993–1997, then reappear in 2015 (dysmenorrhea) and 2023 (cardiometabolic). For bone health, the human trial is 1994, with animal studies spanning 2003–2026. This 20–30 year gap between human studies makes it impossible to know whether older methods, doses, or populations remain relevant; no evidence of replication with contemporary methodology is visible in the records.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The records do not provide any direct information about proposed mechanisms. To assess mechanism, one would need to examine the full texts of these studies to see whether they propose a plausible link (e.g., boron affecting osteoblast differentiation, nuclear factor-κB signaling in immune cells, or steroid hormone receptor activity). The leap from animal bone mineral density changes to human fracture risk, or from rodent TNF-α production to clinical immunocompetence, would need scrutiny, but that scrutiny cannot occur using only the title and design metadata provided here.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that no human outcome has been studied more than twice in the modern era (post-2000), and most have been studied only once. The testosterone trials are from the 1990s, when supplement science was less rigorous; the inflammation RCT (2015, n=113) is single-armed with respect to inflammation outcomes in this record. Animal models of bone health and immune function are known to be poor predictors of human benefit (e.g., many compounds improve rodent bone density without clinical utility). The 'Moderate' grades for inflammation and testosterone rest on 1–2 human trials each, neither of which appears to have been independently replicated.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Preregistered, adequately powered RCTs (n ≥ 200) in contemporary populations, with standardized outcome measures (e.g., bone mineral density via DEXA, validated inflammatory cytokine panels, serum testosterone with proper controls for age and body composition) and at least two independent replicating teams, would be necessary to move any outcome from 'Emerging' or 'Preliminary' to 'Established.' Absent such studies, the evidence should be downgraded to 'Preliminary' across the board due to indirectness (animal-only) and inconsistency (no replicable human signal).

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un elemento mineral que ocurre naturalmente y se encuentra en plantas, suelo y algunos alimentos.
explanation_es.what_it_is: El boro es un elemento químico (símbolo B, número atómico 5) que ocurre naturalmente en el suelo y las plantas. Los humanos lo encuentran principalmente a través de la alimentación — las nueces, verduras de hoja verde, frutas secas y legumbres son fuentes comunes. Las formas de suplemento incluyen citrato de boro, ácido bórico e hidruro de sodio. El elemento en sí no es fabricado por el cuerpo y debe provenir de la dieta o de suplementos.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Probablemente regula la formación ósea y la actividad de células inmunitarias, aunque los mecanismos exactos siguen sin estar claros.
explanation_es.how_it_works: El boro parece desempeñar un papel en cómo se desarrollan las células óseas y en la actividad de las células inmunitarias, pero las vías moleculares precisas aún no se entienden completamente en humanos. Los estudios en animales sugieren que puede influir en el manejo del calcio y el fósforo — minerales críticos para la fortaleza ósea — y puede afectar moléculas de señalización inflamatoria (mensajeros químicos que controlan la inflamación). También puede apoyar el equilibrio hormonal, aunque nuevamente, los mecanismos exactos no están establecidos. Debido a que el boro no ha sido estudiado intensivamente en la bioquímica humana, aún no sabemos cuál de los efectos observados en animales se traduce en personas o cuán importante es el boro bajo condiciones dietéticas normales.
explanation_es.safety_line: El uso oral a corto plazo a dosis moderadas muestra efectos secundarios tolerables; la seguridad a largo plazo y con dosis altas sigue siendo poco estudiada.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos humanos disponibles reportan efectos secundarios leves o nulos a dosis suplementarias (típicamente 3 mg/día o menos), pero estos estudios son cortos e involucran poblaciones pequeñas. Los datos de seguridad a largo plazo son escasos, y la toxicidad a dosis altas (por encima de ~20 mg/día) es un riesgo conocido en modelos animales y exposición ocupacional. La ingesta típica a nivel de alimentos se considera segura, pero la dosificación suplementaria más allá de los niveles dietéticos normales no ha sido validada rigurosamente para la seguridad durante meses o años.
safety_bullets: La suplementación a largo plazo (más allá de semanas) no ha sido probada en ensayos controlados; se desconoce si el uso regular durante meses es seguro.
Las dosis altas (>20 mg/día) conllevan riesgo de toxicidad en modelos animales; los suplementos típicos son mucho más bajos, pero el margen de seguridad en humanos no está establecido.
Ningún estudio recuperado examinó boro en el embarazo, lactancia o niños; la seguridad en estas poblaciones es desconocida.
Ningún estudio de interacción farmacológica adecuadamente potenciado fue recuperado; las posibles interacciones con calcio, magnesio u otros suplementos minerales no han sido probadas.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: El boro es un elemento sólido ligero con solubilidad moderada en agua. Su pequeño tamaño atómico y capacidad de formar fuertes enlaces con oxígeno lo hacen fácilmente incorporado en los huesos y potencialmente activo en la señalización celular. Como mineral dietético, se absorbe en los intestinos y se almacena parcialmente en el hueso; el exceso se excreta en la orina. Este patrón sugiere que se acumula en los tejidos con el tiempo, por lo que los efectos de la dosificación a largo plazo merecen estudio.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ensayo aleatorizado humano de 1994 encontró que la suplementación con boro alteró la densidad mineral ósea y los niveles de calcio/fósforo, pero los resultados completos no se detallan en el resumen. Los estudios en animales (roedores, potrillos y ganado, 2003–2026) reportaron consistentemente una mayor densidad mineral ósea, una estructura ósea más fuerte o un mejor metabolismo óseo después de la dosificación con boro. Los tamaños de muestra en estudios en animales oscilaron entre 10 y 32 animales, y un ensayo humano incluyó participantes, pero la evidencia humana total es solo un pequeño ensayo de hace tres décadas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo existe un estudio humano, lo que hace imposible evaluar la consistencia entre evidencia humana independiente. Los hallazgos en animales son prometedores y consistentes, pero los modelos animales no predicen de manera confiable la respuesta ósea humana. El ensayo humano de 1994 es el único fundamento, y su tamaño de muestra es modesto.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ensayo aleatorizado de 2015 (n=113, mujeres con dolor menstrual) encontró que la suplementación con boro redujo la gravedad y duración del dolor — una proxy para la inflamación. Un ensayo clínico de 2023 examinó los efectos del citrato de boro en marcadores inflamatorios (como citocinas — señales químicas involucradas en la inflamación) y factores metabólicos en humanos, aunque el tamaño de muestra no se indica en el resumen. Cuatro estudios en animales (2001–2026) también mostraron marcadores inflamatorios reducidos o resultados mejorados después del tratamiento con boro. La evidencia humana abarca dos ensayos en aproximadamente 113 participantes verificados en un estudio.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Dos ensayos humanos proporcionan evidencia en poblaciones reales, y los datos en animales corroboran una señal antiinflamatoria. Sin embargo, ningún análisis agrupado confirma que los ensayos estén de acuerdo, y la mayoría de los resúmenes carecen de tamaños de muestra, por lo que la evidencia humana total es incierta. La calificación refleja confianza moderada — mejor que solo en animales, pero aún no lo suficientemente fuerte para llamarlo probado.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro ensayos humanos que abarcan 1993–1997 examinaron el efecto del boro en la testosterona y las hormonas relacionadas en hombres y mujeres. Un ensayo de 1993 analizó la masa corporal magra y la testosterona en culturistas; un RCT de 1994 en hombres midió boro plasmático y testosterona; un ensayo de 1997 examinó factores de riesgo cardiovascular; y un ensayo de 2015 (n=113) en mujeres con dolor menstrual también registró resultados relacionados con hormonas. Los estudios en animales (2014–2022) en cabras y otros modelos reportaron cambios en la función testicular, la calidad del esperma y la actividad tiroidea después de la dosificación con boro. Los tamaños de muestra humana verificados totalizan ~239 en dos de diez estudios; la mayoría de los resúmenes no reportan números, por lo que el tamaño de muestra real es probablemente mucho mayor.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cuatro ensayos humanos proporcionan evidencia del mundo real, y los modelos animales muestran consistentemente efectos relacionados con hormonas. Sin embargo, los estudios abarcan décadas y utilizan diferentes diseños y poblaciones, sin un metanálisis que confirme el acuerdo. La precisión es limitada porque la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra. La calificación moderada refleja evidencia humana genuina compensada por inconsistencia y falta de transparencia en los datos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ocho estudios en animales (2003–2026) en potrillos, cerdos, ratas y ganado examinaron los efectos del boro en medidas inmunitarias — producción de anticuerpos, recuentos de células inmunitarias, producción de interferón y factor de necrosis tumoral-alfa (una molécula de señalización involucrada en la respuesta inmunitaria). Todos reportaron mejoras asociadas con boro en marcadores o resultados inmunitarios. Ningún ensayo humano de función inmunitaria fue recuperado.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia es completamente de modelos animales — roedores, ganado y equinos — ninguno de los cuales son predictores confiables de respuesta inmunitaria humana. Sin datos humanos, el resultado sigue siendo preliminar y especulativo para humanos.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia para el boro está fuertemente orientada hacia estudios en animales (23 en animales o no clasificados, 4 humanos en todos los resultados). Los ensayos humanos son pequeños, principalmente de los años 90 y 2000, o recientes pero con notificación incompleta. Los datos en animales son consistentes y modernos (hasta 2026), sugiriendo interés en investigación en curso, pero la base humana es delgada y anticuada para la salud ósea, limitando la confianza en traducir estos hallazgos a la suplementación típica en personas hoy.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran solo ensayos humanos aislados; no hay revisión sistemática o metanálisis que confirme su acuerdo es visible. La mayoría de los estudios humanos son de hace décadas o recientes pero carecen de detalles publicados sobre el tamaño de muestra y métodos. Los estudios en animales abarcan especies diversas (roedores, potrillos, cabras, cerdos, ganado) y resultados, lo que plantea la pregunta de cuál de los efectos es más relevante para humanos — esta diversidad no fue abordada en los registros recuperados. Los estudios humanos a largo plazo (más allá de semanas) y ensayos de respuesta a la dosis en adultos sanos están completamente ausentes de la muestra. Si el boro es beneficioso solo en estados de deficiencia o si la suplementación por encima de la ingesta dietética proporciona una ventaja real en la población general sigue sin estar claro.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia completa para la utilidad clínica del boro descansa en un puñado de pequeños ensayos humanos de los años 1990–2020; la mayoría de resultados carecen de datos humanos, y el metanálisis es imposible porque ningún estudio parece medir el mismo resultado en la misma población.

concerns.issue: Fragmentación severa de la evidencia; no es posible agrupar datos
concerns.detail: Entre cuatro resultados, solo se citan 6 estudios humanos, y ninguno de ellos aparece en múltiples resultados simultáneamente. Los resultados de inflamación y testosterona citan cada uno 1–2 ensayos humanos separados por décadas (1993–2023), lo que hace imposible evaluar la consistencia o realizar metanálisis. El motor anotó explícitamente 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble' para cada resultado. Este no es un problema menor—significa que ninguna síntesis cuantitativa respalda ninguna calificación.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de la evidencia es solo en animales, con validez de traslación no probada
concerns.detail: La función inmunológica es 100% en animales (8/8 estudios); la salud ósea es 83% en animales (5/6); la testosterona es 60% en animales (6/10); solo la inflamación se aproxima al equilibrio con 67% en animales (4/6). El motor señaló la función inmunológica como indirectamente relevante para humanos porque es solo en animales. Ninguna evidencia en estos registros demuestra que los efectos del boro en órganos inmunológicos de roedores, densidad mineral ósea en potros, o función testicular en cabras se traduzcan en beneficio clínico humano.

concerns.issue: Subestimación crónica de tamaños de muestra y datos faltantes
concerns.detail: Para la salud ósea, solo 2 de 6 estudios reportan n; para la función inmunológica, solo 2 de 8; para la inflamación, solo 1 de 6; para la testosterona, solo 2 de 10. El motor señala que 'el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor' para algunos resultados, pero los registros no muestran cuál es ese total. Esta opacidad impide evaluar si la base de evidencia está realmente potenciada o si estudios con n baja están impulsando las conclusiones.

concerns.issue: Un único ensayo humano tiene peso desproporcionado para la salud ósea
concerns.detail: La calificación 'Emergente' para la salud ósea descansa en gran medida en un ECA de 1994 (el único ensayo humano nombrado explícitamente). El motor anotó 'solo un estudio humano aborda este resultado; la consistencia no puede evaluarse entre evidencia humana independiente.' Han pasado treinta años sin replicación. Un único ensayo pequeño de 1994 no es base suficiente para una calificación en ningún resultado en síntesis de evidencia moderna.

concerns.issue: Agrupamiento temporal y posible sesgo de publicación o desviación metodológica
concerns.detail: Dentro de testosterona/hormonas, los ECA humanos se agrupan en 1993–1997, luego reaparecen en 2015 (dismenorrea) y 2023 (cardiometabólico). Para la salud ósea, el ensayo humano es de 1994, con estudios en animales abarcando 2003–2026. Esta brecha de 20–30 años entre estudios humanos hace imposible saber si métodos, dosis o poblaciones más antiguos siguen siendo relevantes; no hay evidencia de replicación con metodología contemporánea visible en los registros.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Los registros no proporcionan información directa sobre mecanismos propuestos. Para evaluar el mecanismo, sería necesario examinar los textos completos de estos estudios para ver si proponen un vínculo plausible (p. ej., boro afectando la diferenciación de osteoblastos, señalización del factor nuclear-κB en células inmunológicas, o actividad de receptores de hormonas esteroides). El salto de cambios en densidad mineral ósea en animales a riesgo de fractura en humanos, o de producción de TNF-α en roedores a inmunocompetencia clínica, requeriría un examen riguroso, pero ese examen no puede ocurrir usando solo los metadatos de título y diseño proporcionados aquí.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que ningún resultado humano ha sido estudiado más de dos veces en la era moderna (posterior a 2000), y la mayoría solo ha sido estudiada una vez. Los ensayos de testosterona son de los años 1990, cuando la ciencia de suplementos era menos rigurosa; el ECA de inflamación (2015, n=113) es de un solo brazo respecto a resultados de inflamación en este registro. Se sabe que los modelos animales de salud ósea y función inmunológica son malos predictores de beneficio humano (p. ej., muchos compuestos mejoran la densidad ósea en roedores sin utilidad clínica). Las calificaciones 'Moderada' para inflamación y testosterona descansan en 1–2 ensayos humanos cada una, ninguno de los cuales parece haber sido replicado independientemente.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: ECA preregistrados, adecuadamente potenciados (n ≥ 200) en poblaciones contemporáneas, con medidas de resultado estandarizadas (p. ej., densidad mineral ósea por DEXA, paneles de citocinas inflamatorias validados, testosterona sérica con controles apropiados para edad y composición corporal) y al menos dos equipos replicadores independientes, serían necesarios para mover cualquier resultado de 'Emergente' o 'Preliminar' a 'Establecido.' En ausencia de tales estudios, la evidencia debe ser degradada a 'Preliminar' en toda la tabla debido a indirectividad (solo animales) e inconsistencia (sin señal humana replicable).
